reason: Both pages are candid that the A1C results come from a small group, which I'd want to see. A is a bit more careful: it adds that these customers chose to share their results and doesn't tie the 0.6-point average only to the 10 whose A1C went down, while B's wording reads as if it does. That makes A slightly easier to trust before paying $59, even though B's lines about cancelling if it doesn't help speak to my history of quitting.
